item.text: {"0":"Feature construction: multiply each existing item input embedding by 1 + 0.1*log1p(c), where c counts earlier occurrences of that item in the causal user prefix. Compute counts before context truncation and use identical logic at inference. This bounded-strength repeat signal may help the GRU distinguish recurring interests without changing embedding parameters, topology, readout, loss or optimizer. Apply to all four categories, retaining one model per category.","1":"Network architecture: add one same-width GRU layer with a residual connection from its input to its output, retaining the existing final-state readout and scoring mechanism. The additional recurrent transformation may capture higher-order purchase patterns while the residual path preserves useful representations and gradient flow. Keep features, embeddings, context selection, loss and optimizer fixed across all four category models.","2":"Sequence modeling: restrict each causal input to its most recent 20 interactions, preserving chronological order and using the same truncation in training and prediction. Shorter context may reduce interference from stale purchases and improve next-item HR@10, particularly in Electronics. Keep supplied splits, features, embeddings, GRU topology, readout, loss and optimizer fixed; train one model for each of the four categories.","3":"Training strategy: keep the baseline optimizer and initial learning rate, but apply cosine learning-rate decay to 10% of that rate over the existing 200-epoch cap. Smaller later updates may stabilize validation ranking as training loss continues falling. Preserve baseline early stopping, batch size, dropout, weight decay, architecture and loss, with seed 42 and one trained model per category across all four categories."}
